## Masking makes every mode talk to its neighbours {.nka-slide data-prevent-swipe="true"}

```{=html}
<div id="nka-root">

<!-- Seven content-free reveal fragments drive the eight steps, so the arrow keys
     walk them like slides. The state machine listens for fragmentshown /
     fragmenthidden and redraws. -->
<span class="fragment nka-step" data-fragment-index="0"></span>
<span class="fragment nka-step" data-fragment-index="1"></span>
<span class="fragment nka-step" data-fragment-index="2"></span>
<span class="fragment nka-step" data-fragment-index="3"></span>
<span class="fragment nka-step" data-fragment-index="4"></span>
<span class="fragment nka-step" data-fragment-index="5"></span>
<span class="fragment nka-step" data-fragment-index="6"></span>

<div class="nka-cap" id="nka-cap"></div>

<div class="nka-eq">
  <div id="eq0">\(a(x)\)</div>
  <div id="eq1">\(\tilde a(x)=w(x)\,a(x)\)</div>
  <div id="eq2">\(\tilde a_k=\sum_{k'} W_{k-k'}\,a_{k'}\)</div>
  <div id="eq3">\(\langle \tilde C_k\rangle=\sum_{k'} M_{kk'}\,C_{k'}\)</div>
  <div id="eq4">\(\langle \hat C_k\rangle = M^{-1}\langle \tilde C_k\rangle = C_k\)</div>
  <div id="eq5">\({\rm Cov}\propto\big|\textstyle\sum_{k''} W_{k-k''}W^{*}_{k'-k''}C_{k''}\big|^{2}\)</div>
  <div id="eq6">\({\rm Cov}\simeq C_{\bar k}C_{\bar k}\,\Xi_{kk'}(w_aw_c,w_bw_d)\)</div>
</div>

<div id="scene1">
  <svg id="svgA" viewBox="0 0 1730 300" width="1730" height="300"></svg>
  <svg id="svgB" viewBox="0 0 1730 350" width="1730" height="350"></svg>
</div>

<div id="sceneZoo" class="hidden">
  <svg id="svgZ" viewBox="0 0 1730 660" width="1730" height="660"></svg>
</div>

<div id="scene2" class="hidden">
  <div style="display:flex; gap:34px; align-items:flex-start;" id="mrow">
    <div class="mcell" id="wE"><canvas id="cvE" style="width:360px;height:360px"></canvas>
      <div class="mlab"><b>exact</b>direct sum<br><span style="font-size:24px">k, k' = 6 … 155</span></div></div>
    <div class="mcell" id="wN"><canvas id="cvN" style="width:360px;height:360px"></canvas>
      <div class="mlab"><b>NKA</b>one mask-product kernel</div></div>
    <div class="mcell" id="wD"><canvas id="cvD" style="width:360px;height:360px"></canvas>
      <div class="mlab"><b>NKA &minus; exact</b>error</div></div>
  </div>
  <svg id="svgC" viewBox="0 0 1730 250" width="1730" height="250"></svg>
</div>

<div id="nka-side"></div>

<div class="nka-ctl">
  <div class="nka-mask hidden" id="mwrap">
    <label>mask width<input id="sWidth" type="range" min="4" max="70" value="16"></label>
    <label>holes<input id="sHoles" type="range" min="0" max="6" value="0"></label>
    <label>apodization<input id="sApod" type="range" min="2" max="90" value="30"></label>
  </div>
  <span class="dots" id="dots"></span>
  <button id="prev">&larr;</button>
  <button id="next">&rarr;</button>
</div>
</div>

<script>
(function(){
  var R = document.getElementById('nka-root');
  if(!R) return;

  // ---------- config ----------
  var N   = 512;             // signed mode index -N/2 .. N/2-1
  var NX  = 1024;            // real-space samples
  var KLO = 6, KHI = 156;    // modes shown in the covariance matrices
  var NK  = KHI - KLO;       // 150
  var KMAX = 250;            // modes drawn in the harmonic panel
  var KP   = 250;            // modes in the coupling matrix we actually invert

  // the working mask: width, number of holes, apodization length (all fractions of L)
  var mW = 0.16, mH = 0, mA = 0.030;
  var k0 = 78;               // where the kernel sits — draggable

  // A pronounced bump gives the slide two regimes: the smooth falling part, where
  // C is flat across the kernel and the NKA holds, and the bump, where it does not.
  function Cfun(k){ var a = Math.abs(k);
    return (1.0/Math.pow(1.0 + a/18.0, 1.6)) * (1 + 2.5*Math.exp(-Math.pow((a-78)/6,2))); }

  // deterministic PRNG
  function mulberry(a){ return function(){
    a |= 0; a = a + 0x6D2B79F5 | 0;
    var t = Math.imul(a ^ a >>> 15, 1 | a);
    t = t + Math.imul(t ^ t >>> 7, 61 | t) ^ t;
    return ((t ^ t >>> 14) >>> 0) / 4294967296; }; }
  function gauss(rng){
    var u = 1 - rng(), v = rng();
    return Math.sqrt(-2*Math.log(u)) * Math.cos(2*Math.PI*v); }

  // ---------- realise one Gaussian field a(x) (fixed seed) ----------
  var field = new Float64Array(NX);
  (function(){
    var rng = mulberry(20260903);
    for(var k=1;k<N/2;k++){
      var s = Math.sqrt(Cfun(k)/2), re = gauss(rng)*s, im = gauss(rng)*s;
      for(var j=0;j<NX;j++){
        var ph = 2*Math.PI*k*j/NX;
        field[j] += 2*(re*Math.cos(ph) - im*Math.sin(ph));
      }
    }
    var mx = 0; for(var j2=0;j2<NX;j2++) mx = Math.max(mx, Math.abs(field[j2]));
    for(var j3=0;j3<NX;j3++) field[j3] /= mx;   // scale to [-1,1] for drawing
  })();

  // ---------- masks ----------
  //  A C2 cosine (Hann) ramp of length `apod` on every edge — of the footprint and
  //  of every hole. Apodization is the lever that suppresses the kernel's sidelobes,
  //  so it has to be visible as a ramp, not a hairline.
  function ramp(t){ return 0.5*(1 - Math.cos(Math.PI*Math.max(0,Math.min(1,t)))); }

  function makeMask(width, nholes, apod){
    var w = new Float64Array(NX), ap = Math.max(apod*NX, 1);
    var half = width*NX/2, mid = NX/2;
    for(var j=0;j<NX;j++){
      var d = Math.abs(j - mid);
      w[j] = ramp((half - d)/ap + 0.5);
    }
    if(nholes > 0){
      // holes at fixed pseudo-random positions inside the footprint, each apodized
      var rng = mulberry(4242), inner = width*NX - 2*ap;
      for(var h=0; h<nholes; h++){
        var hw = Math.max(inner/(3.2*nholes), 2*ap*0.6);
        var c  = mid - inner/2 + (h + 0.15 + 0.7*rng())*inner/nholes;
        for(var j2=0;j2<NX;j2++){
          var dd = Math.abs(j2 - c);
          w[j2] *= 1 - ramp((hw/2 - dd)/ap + 0.5);
        }
      }
    }
    return w;
  }

  // ---------- transforms ----------
  var COS = new Float64Array(NX), SIN = new Float64Array(NX);
  for(var t0=0;t0<NX;t0++){ COS[t0]=Math.cos(2*Math.PI*t0/NX); SIN[t0]=Math.sin(2*Math.PI*t0/NX); }

  function transform(w, nmodes){
    var re = new Float64Array(nmodes), im = new Float64Array(nmodes), sp = 0;
    for(var mi=0; mi<nmodes; mi++){
      var m = mi < nmodes/2 ? mi : mi - nmodes, sr = 0, si = 0;
      for(var jj=0; jj<NX; jj++){
        var idx = (m*jj) % NX; if(idx < 0) idx += NX;
        sr += w[jj]*COS[idx]; si -= w[jj]*SIN[idx];
      }
      re[mi] = sr/NX; im[mi] = si/NX;
      sp += re[mi]*re[mi] + im[mi]*im[mi];
    }
    return {re:re, im:im, sumP:sp};
  }

  var mask = null, Wre = null, Wim = null, sumP = 1;
  function Wat(m, part){
    if(m <= -N/2 || m >= N/2) return 0;
    var i = (m + N) % N;
    return part ? Wim[i] : Wre[i];
  }
  function kernelPower(m){ var r = Wat(m,0), i = Wat(m,1); return r*r + i*i; }

  // ---------- derived quantities ----------
  var Cin = new Float64Array(KMAX+2), Ctil = new Float64Array(KMAX+2);
  var covE = new Float64Array(NK*NK), covN = new Float64Array(NK*NK);

  // Decoupling is done in BANDPOWERS, because the unbinned coupling matrix is not
  // invertible in any useful sense: the symbol of the Toeplitz operator M is the
  // mask squared, so every mode the mask kills is a null direction. Binning to
  // roughly the kernel width is exactly what NaMaster does, and what makes the
  // inverse well posed.
  var NB = 6, NBIN = Math.floor(KP/NB);
  var Cdecb = new Float64Array(NBIN), Ctrueb = new Float64Array(NBIN);
  function binCentre(b){ return 1 + b*NB + (NB-1)/2; }

  function buildAll(){
    mask = makeMask(mW, mH, mA);
    var T = transform(mask, N); Wre = T.re; Wim = T.im; sumP = T.sumP;

    for(var k=1;k<=KMAX;k++){
      Cin[k] = Cfun(k);
      var acc = 0;
      for(var kp=-N/2; kp<N/2; kp++) acc += kernelPower(k-kp)*Cfun(kp);
      Ctil[k] = acc/sumP;                       // <Ctil> = M C, full sum
    }
    decouple();
    covariances();
  }

  // Mb_{bb'} = (1/NB) sum_{k in b} sum_{k' in b'} |W_{k-k'}|^2 / sumP,
  // then solve Mb x = <Ctil>_b.  x comes back as the binned true spectrum.
  function decouple(){
    var n = NBIN, A = new Float64Array(n*n), b = new Float64Array(n);
    for(var i=0;i<n;i++){
      for(var j=0;j<n;j++){
        var acc = 0;
        for(var k=0;k<NB;k++) for(var kp=0;kp<NB;kp++)
          acc += kernelPower((1+i*NB+k) - (1+j*NB+kp));
        A[i*n+j] = acc/(NB*sumP);
      }
      var st = 0, tr = 0;
      for(var k2=0;k2<NB;k2++){ st += Ctil[1+i*NB+k2]; tr += Cfun(1+i*NB+k2); }
      b[i] = st/NB; Ctrueb[i] = tr/NB;
    }
    // Gauss-Jordan with partial pivoting
    for(var c=0;c<n;c++){
      var piv = c, best = Math.abs(A[c*n+c]);
      for(var r=c+1;r<n;r++){ var v = Math.abs(A[r*n+c]); if(v>best){best=v;piv=r;} }
      if(best < 1e-13){ for(var z=0;z<n;z++) Cdecb[z] = NaN; return; }
      if(piv !== c){
        for(var q=0;q<n;q++){ var tm=A[c*n+q]; A[c*n+q]=A[piv*n+q]; A[piv*n+q]=tm; }
        var tb=b[c]; b[c]=b[piv]; b[piv]=tb;
      }
      var d = A[c*n+c];
      for(var q2=c;q2<n;q2++) A[c*n+q2] /= d;
      b[c] /= d;
      for(var r2=0;r2<n;r2++){
        if(r2===c) continue;
        var f = A[r2*n+c];
        if(f === 0) continue;
        for(var q3=c;q3<n;q3++) A[r2*n+q3] -= f*A[c*n+q3];
        b[r2] -= f*b[c];
      }
    }
    for(var o=0;o<n;o++) Cdecb[o] = b[o];
  }

  function covariances(){
    var Xre = new Float64Array(2*N), Xim = new Float64Array(2*N);
    for(var d=-N+1; d<N; d++){
      var ar=0, ai=0;
      for(var m=-N/2; m<N/2; m++){
        var wr1=Wat(d+m,0), wi1=Wat(d+m,1), wr2=Wat(m,0), wi2=Wat(m,1);
        ar += wr1*wr2 + wi1*wi2;
        ai += wi1*wr2 - wr1*wi2;
      }
      Xre[d+N]=ar; Xim[d+N]=ai;
    }
    var n2 = sumP*sumP;
    var Ar = new Float64Array(NK*N), Ai = new Float64Array(NK*N);
    var Br = new Float64Array(NK*N), Bi = new Float64Array(NK*N);
    for(var i=0;i<NK;i++){
      var k = KLO + i;
      for(var qi=0; qi<N; qi++){
        var q = qi - N/2;
        var wr = Wat(k-q,0), wi = Wat(k-q,1), c = Cfun(q);
        Ar[i*N+qi] = wr*c; Ai[i*N+qi] = wi*c;
        Br[i*N+qi] = wr;   Bi[i*N+qi] = wi;
      }
    }
    for(var a=0;a<NK;a++){
      var ka = KLO + a, oa = a*N;
      for(var b=0;b<NK;b++){
        var kb = KLO + b, ob = b*N, sr=0, si=0;
        for(var p=0;p<N;p++){
          var x1r=Ar[oa+p], x1i=Ai[oa+p], x2r=Br[ob+p], x2i=Bi[ob+p];
          sr += x1r*x2r + x1i*x2i;
          si += x1i*x2r - x1r*x2i;
        }
        covE[a*NK+b] = 2*(sr*sr + si*si)/n2;
        var cb = Cfun((ka+kb)/2), dd = ka-kb+N;
        var nr = cb*Xre[dd], ni = cb*Xim[dd];
        covN[a*NK+b] = 2*(nr*nr + ni*ni)/n2;
      }
    }
  }

  // ---------- drawing helpers ----------
  var NS = 'http://www.w3.org/2000/svg';
  function el(p, t, at){ var e = document.createElementNS(NS,t);
    for(var k in at) e.setAttribute(k, at[k]); p.appendChild(e); return e; }
  function txt(p, x, y, s, at){ var e = el(p,'text',
      Object.assign({x:x,y:y,'font-size':26,fill:'#1B1611'}, at||{}));
    e.textContent = s; return e; }

  function divergent(v){                       // ground -> cobalt / cinnabar
    var t = Math.max(-1, Math.min(1, v));
    if(t >= 0){ var u = Math.pow(t,0.55);
      return [247 - 186*u, 240 - 149*u, 225 - 65*u]; }
    var u2 = Math.pow(-t,0.55);
    return [247 - 59*u2, 240 - 171*u2, 225 - 169*u2];
  }
  function heat(cv, mat, scale){
    cv.width = NK; cv.height = NK;
    var ctx = cv.getContext('2d'), im = ctx.createImageData(NK,NK);
    for(var i=0;i<NK;i++) for(var j=0;j<NK;j++){
      var c = divergent(mat[i*NK+j]/scale), o = 4*(i*NK+j);
      im.data[o]=c[0]; im.data[o+1]=c[1]; im.data[o+2]=c[2]; im.data[o+3]=255;
    }
    ctx.putImageData(im,0,0);
  }

  // Effective coupling width: full width of the smallest symmetric window in
  // |W_m|^2 holding half the kernel power. Half-maximum is useless here — a
  // complex mask gives a narrow spike on a broad skirt, and FWHM reports 1 while
  // modes tens apart are still strongly coupled. Same definition as slides 3 & 5.
  //   The m = 0 self-coupling carries most of |W|^2 for any mask, so including it
  //   makes every mask look narrow. What we want is the reach of the OFF-diagonal
  //   coupling: how far a mode talks to modes that are not itself.
  function powerWidth(pow, mmax){
    var tot = 0, m;
    for(m=1;m<=mmax;m++) tot += 2*pow(m);
    if(tot <= 0) return 1;
    var acc = 0, n = 0;
    while(acc < 0.5*tot && n < mmax){ n++; acc += pow(-n) + pow(n); }
    return Math.max(2*n, 1);
  }

  // The span the kernel actually couples over, and the peak for scaling the draw.
  // It uses the off-diagonal power width, not half-maximum: with a complex mask the
  // kernel is a spike on a broad skirt, and half-maximum would report a couple of
  // modes while the covariance is visibly wrong — the two readouts have to agree.
  function kernelSpan(){
    var pk = 0, m;
    for(m=-N/2+1;m<N/2;m++) pk = Math.max(pk, kernelPower(m));
    var hw = powerWidth(kernelPower, N/2-1)/2;
    return {lo:-hw, hi:hw, pk:pk};
  }
  // The error the NKA actually makes, stated exactly: it replaces the
  // kernel-weighted average of C by C at the midpoint. Returns the fractional
  // difference between the two. (max/min across the span is the wrong statistic —
  // at the peak of a bump C hardly "varies" either side yet the midpoint value
  // sits well above the average, which is precisely when the NKA fails.)
  function pullOutError(kc){
    var num = 0, den = 0;
    for(var m=-N/2+1;m<N/2;m++){
      var p = kernelPower(m), kk = kc - m;
      if(kk < 1) continue;
      num += p*Cfun(kk); den += p;
    }
    if(den <= 0) return 0;
    return Cfun(kc)/(num/den) - 1;
  }
  function pct(x){ return (x>=0?'+':'') + (100*x).toFixed(0) + '%'; }

  // ---------- panel A: real space ----------
  var PAD = 90, W1 = 1730, AW = W1 - PAD - 40;
  function drawA(step){
    var s = document.getElementById('svgA'); s.innerHTML = '';
    var y0 = 62, h = 200, mid = y0 + h/2;
    el(s,'line',{x1:PAD,y1:mid,x2:PAD+AW,y2:mid,stroke:'#C5B89E','stroke-width':2});
    txt(s, 10, mid+9, 'a(x)', {fill:'#7A6F5C'});
    txt(s, PAD, 294, 'position  x', {fill:'#7A6F5C','font-size':26});

    if(step >= 1){
      // the mask as a filled window function — the taper is the point, so it is
      // drawn as an area under the curve rather than as a box
      var d = 'M ' + PAD + ' ' + (y0+h);
      for(var j=0;j<NX;j++)
        d += ' L ' + (PAD + AW*j/(NX-1)).toFixed(1) + ' ' + (y0 + h - mask[j]*h*0.94).toFixed(1);
      d += ' L ' + (PAD+AW) + ' ' + (y0+h) + ' Z';
      el(s,'path',{d:d,fill:'#3D5BA0',opacity:0.13});
      var d2 = '';
      for(var j2=0;j2<NX;j2++)
        d2 += (j2?'L':'M') + (PAD + AW*j2/(NX-1)).toFixed(1) + ' ' + (y0 + h - mask[j2]*h*0.94).toFixed(1) + ' ';
      el(s,'path',{d:d2,fill:'none',stroke:'#3D5BA0','stroke-width':3});
      txt(s, PAD+AW-250, y0 + 26, 'mask  w(x)', {fill:'#3D5BA0','font-size':28});
    }
    function path(scaleByMask, col, wid){
      var d = '';
      for(var j=0;j<NX;j++){
        var v = field[j]*(scaleByMask ? mask[j] : 1);
        d += (j?'L':'M') + (PAD + AW*j/(NX-1)).toFixed(1) + ' ' + (mid - v*h*0.44).toFixed(1) + ' ';
      }
      el(s,'path',{d:d,fill:'none',stroke:col,'stroke-width':wid});
    }
    if(step >= 1){
      path(false,'#C5B89E',2); path(true,'#1B1611',3);
      var ly = y0 - 22;
      el(s,'line',{x1:PAD,y1:ly-8,x2:PAD+46,y2:ly-8,stroke:'#C5B89E','stroke-width':3});
      txt(s, PAD+58, ly, 'field  a', {fill:'#9C8F79','font-size':28});
      el(s,'line',{x1:PAD+230,y1:ly-8,x2:PAD+276,y2:ly-8,stroke:'#1B1611','stroke-width':3});
      txt(s, PAD+288, ly, 'observed  w·a', {fill:'#1B1611','font-size':28});
    }
    else path(false,'#1B1611',3);
  }

  // ---------- panel B: harmonic space ----------
  var By0 = 14, Bh = 272, Bkmax = KMAX;
  function BX(k){ return PAD + AW*(k-1)/(Bkmax-1); }
  function Bk(x){ return 1 + (x - PAD)*(Bkmax-1)/AW; }
  function drawB(step){
    var s = document.getElementById('svgB'); s.innerHTML = '';
    var lgmin = Math.log10(Cfun(Bkmax)), lgmax = Math.log10(Cfun(78));
    function Y(c){ return By0 + Bh*(1 - (Math.log10(c)-lgmin)/(lgmax-lgmin)); }
    el(s,'line',{x1:PAD,y1:By0+Bh,x2:PAD+AW,y2:By0+Bh,stroke:'#C5B89E','stroke-width':2});
    txt(s, PAD, By0+Bh+44, 'wavenumber  k', {fill:'#7A6F5C'});
    txt(s, 4, By0+18, 'Cₖ', {fill:'#7A6F5C'});

    var d1='', d2='';
    for(var k=1;k<Bkmax;k++){
      d1 += (k>1?'L':'M') + BX(k).toFixed(1) + ' ' + Y(Cin[k]).toFixed(1) + ' ';
      d2 += (k>1?'L':'M') + BX(k).toFixed(1) + ' ' + Y(Ctil[k]).toFixed(1) + ' ';
    }
    el(s,'path',{d:d1,fill:'none',stroke:'#1B1611','stroke-width':3.5});
    txt(s, BX(150), Y(Cin[150])-26, 'true  Cₖ', {fill:'#1B1611','font-size':28});

    if(step >= 4){
      el(s,'path',{d:d2,fill:'none',stroke:'#BC4538','stroke-width':3.5,
                   'stroke-dasharray':'10 7'});
      txt(s, BX(150), Y(Ctil[150])+50, 'masked  C̃ₖ', {fill:'#BC4538','font-size':28});
    }
    if(step >= 5){
      // the decoupled bandpowers, landing back on the truth
      for(var bi=0; bi<NBIN; bi++){
        var kc = binCentre(bi);
        if(kc < 8 || kc > Bkmax-22) continue;
        if(!isFinite(Cdecb[bi]) || Cdecb[bi] <= 0) continue;
        el(s,'circle',{cx:BX(kc),cy:Y(Cdecb[bi]),r:7,fill:'#3F8278'});
      }
      txt(s, BX(150), Y(Cfun(150))-84, 'decoupled bandpowers  M⁻¹C̃', {fill:'#3F8278','font-size':28});
    }
    if(step < 3) return;

    // the kernel, parked at k0 — draggable
    var span = kernelSpan(), dk = '';
    for(var m=-N/2+1;m<N/2;m++){
      var kk = k0 - m; if(kk < 0.5 || kk > Bkmax) continue;
      dk += (dk?'L':'M') + BX(kk).toFixed(1) + ' ' + (By0+Bh - 150*kernelPower(m)/span.pk).toFixed(1) + ' ';
    }
    el(s,'path',{d:dk,fill:'none',stroke:'#3D5BA0','stroke-width':3.5});
    var lo = Math.max(k0 - span.hi, 1), hi = Math.min(k0 - span.lo, Bkmax-1);
    el(s,'rect',{x:BX(lo),y:By0,width:Math.max(BX(hi)-BX(lo),3),height:Bh,
                 fill:'#3D5BA0',opacity:0.10});
    // the readout lives in a fixed corner: parked next to the kernel it collides
    // with whichever part of the spectrum the kernel is sitting on
    var v = pullOutError(k0), bad = Math.abs(v) > 0.05, lx = PAD + AW - 560;
    txt(s, lx, By0+26, 'kernel  |W|²  — drag me along k', {fill:'#3D5BA0','font-size':28});
    txt(s, lx, By0+64, 'C at k₀ vs its kernel average:  ' + pct(v),
        {fill: bad ? '#BC4538' : '#3D5BA0', 'font-size':28});
  }

  // ---------- the mask zoo: complexity, not size alone ----------
  var ZOO = [
    {w:0.55, h:0, a:0.070, name:'wide, smoothly apodized'},
    {w:0.16, h:0, a:0.030, name:'small'},
    {w:0.55, h:5, a:0.010, name:'holes and sharp edges'}
  ];
  function drawZoo(){
    var s = document.getElementById('svgZ'); s.innerHTML='';
    var MW = 720, KW = 780, KX = PAD + MW + 110;
    for(var r=0;r<ZOO.length;r++){
      var z = ZOO[r], y = 86 + r*192, h = 116;
      var w = makeMask(z.w, z.h, z.a), T = transform(w, N);
      // mask
      var d = 'M ' + PAD + ' ' + (y+h);
      for(var j=0;j<NX;j++) d += ' L ' + (PAD + MW*j/(NX-1)).toFixed(1) + ' ' + (y + h - w[j]*h).toFixed(1);
      d += ' L ' + (PAD+MW) + ' ' + (y+h) + ' Z';
      el(s,'path',{d:d,fill:'#3D5BA0',opacity:0.13});
      var d2='';
      for(var j2=0;j2<NX;j2++) d2 += (j2?'L':'M') + (PAD + MW*j2/(NX-1)).toFixed(1) + ' ' + (y + h - w[j2]*h).toFixed(1) + ' ';
      el(s,'path',{d:d2,fill:'none',stroke:'#3D5BA0','stroke-width':3});
      txt(s, PAD, y - 14, z.name, {fill:'#7A6F5C','font-size':27});
      // kernel, log power so the sidelobes show
      var pk = 0, MM = 60, p = [];
      for(var m=-MM;m<=MM;m++){
        var i = (m + N) % N, v = T.re[i]*T.re[i] + T.im[i]*T.im[i];
        p.push(v); if(v>pk) pk=v;
      }
      el(s,'line',{x1:KX,y1:y+h,x2:KX+KW,y2:y+h,stroke:'#C5B89E','stroke-width':2});
      var dk='';
      for(var q=0;q<p.length;q++){
        var lg = Math.log10(Math.max(p[q]/pk, 1e-5))/5 + 1;     // 0 at 1e-5, 1 at peak
        dk += (q?'L':'M') + (KX + KW*q/(p.length-1)).toFixed(1) + ' ' + (y + h - lg*h).toFixed(1) + ' ';
      }
      el(s,'path',{d:dk,fill:'none',stroke:'#BC4538','stroke-width':3});
      var wid = powerWidth(function(m){ var i=(m+N)%N; return T.re[i]*T.re[i]+T.im[i]*T.im[i]; }, MM);
      var cq = (p.length-1)/2, hw = wid/2;
      el(s,'line',{x1:KX + KW*(cq-hw)/(p.length-1),y1:y+h+24,
                   x2:KX + KW*(cq+hw)/(p.length-1),y2:y+h+24,
                   stroke:'#BC4538','stroke-width':8,'stroke-linecap':'round'});
      txt(s, KX + KW*(cq+hw)/(p.length-1) + 20, y+h+34, wid + ' modes',
          {fill:'#BC4538','font-size':27});
    }
    txt(s, PAD, 30, 'mask  w(x)', {fill:'#3D5BA0','font-size':29});
    txt(s, KX, 30, 'kernel  |W|²   (log)', {fill:'#BC4538','font-size':29});
  }

  // ---------- panel C: C across the kernel (scene 2) ----------
  function drawC(){
    var s = document.getElementById('svgC'); s.innerHTML='';
    var x0 = PAD, y0 = 22, h = 132, w = AW, kmax = KMAX;
    var lgmin = Math.log10(Cfun(kmax)), lgmax = Math.log10(Cfun(78));
    function X(k){ return x0 + w*(k-1)/(kmax-1); }
    function Y(c){ return y0 + h*(1 - (Math.log10(c)-lgmin)/(lgmax-lgmin)); }
    var d='';
    for(var k=1;k<kmax;k++) d += (k>1?'L':'M')+X(k).toFixed(1)+' '+Y(Cfun(k)).toFixed(1)+' ';
    el(s,'path',{d:d,fill:'none',stroke:'#1B1611','stroke-width':3.5});
    var span = kernelSpan(), dk='';
    for(var m=-N/2+1;m<N/2;m++){
      var kk = k0 - m; if(kk<0.5||kk>kmax) continue;
      dk += (dk?'L':'M')+X(kk).toFixed(1)+' '+(y0+h-90*kernelPower(m)/span.pk).toFixed(1)+' ';
    }
    el(s,'path',{d:dk,fill:'none',stroke:'#3D5BA0','stroke-width':3.5});
    var lo = Math.max(k0-span.hi,1), hi = Math.min(k0-span.lo,kmax-1);
    el(s,'rect',{x:X(lo),y:y0,width:Math.max(X(hi)-X(lo),3),height:h,fill:'#3D5BA0',opacity:0.12});
    var v = pullOutError(k0), bad = Math.abs(v) > 0.05;
    el(s,'line',{x1:X(lo),y1:y0+h+28,x2:X(hi),y2:y0+h+28,
                 stroke: bad?'#BC4538':'#3D5BA0','stroke-width':4});
    txt(s, X(hi)+22, y0+h+38, 'C at k₀ vs its kernel average:  ' + pct(v),
        {fill: bad?'#BC4538':'#3D5BA0','font-size':28});
    // live NKA error on the covariance diagonal at the kernel's location
    var ik = Math.round(k0) - KLO;
    if(ik >= 0 && ik < NK){
      var e = covN[ik*NK+ik]/covE[ik*NK+ik] - 1;
      txt(s, X(1), y0+h+38, 'NKA error at k₀: ' + (100*e).toFixed(1) + '%',
          {fill: Math.abs(e)>0.05 ? '#BC4538' : '#7A6F5C','font-size':28});
    }
  }

  function drawMatrices(){
    var rE = new Float64Array(NK*NK), rN = new Float64Array(NK*NK),
        rD = new Float64Array(NK*NK), d = new Float64Array(NK);
    for(var i=0;i<NK;i++) d[i] = Math.sqrt(covE[i*NK+i]);
    for(var a=0;a<NK;a++) for(var b=0;b<NK;b++){
      var q = a*NK+b, nrm = d[a]*d[b];
      rE[q] = covE[q]/nrm; rN[q] = covN[q]/nrm; rD[q] = rN[q]-rE[q];
    }
    heat(document.getElementById('cvE'), rE, 1);
    heat(document.getElementById('cvN'), rN, 1);
    heat(document.getElementById('cvD'), rD, 0.35);
  }

  // ---------- step machine ----------
  var CAPS = [
    'one field, modes independent',
    'we only see part of it — and the mask is apodized',
    'complexity, not size: holes and sharp edges widen the kernel',
    'mask × field  →  kernel ∗ modes',
    'the kernel smears the spectrum',
    'the estimator is exact: invert the coupling',
    'the error bar needs a four-point sum',
    'narrow-kernel approximation: pull C out, one kernel is left'
  ];
  // The cost, as a running label: the exact four-point sum, then what the NKA
  // buys you. Written as HTML because MathJax has already typeset the page.
  var COST = ['','','','','','',
              '<i>O</i>(k<sub>max</sub><sup>6</sup>)',
              '<i>O</i>(k<sub>max</sub><sup>3</sup>) — same as the estimator'];
  var NSTEP = 8, step = 0;
  var caps = document.getElementById('nka-cap'), side = document.getElementById('nka-side');
  var dots = document.getElementById('dots');
  for(var i=0;i<NSTEP;i++) dots.appendChild(document.createElement('span'));

  // Each equation appears with the concept it names, and stays.
  var EQ_STEP = [0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7];
  function equations(){
    for(var i=0;i<EQ_STEP.length;i++){
      var e = document.getElementById('eq'+i);
      e.style.display = (step >= EQ_STEP[i]) ? '' : 'none';
      var live = (EQ_STEP[i] === step) || (i === 6 && step >= 7);
      e.className = live ? 'on' : '';
    }
  }

  function render(){
    caps.innerHTML = CAPS[step]; side.innerHTML = COST[step];
    equations();
    var zoo = (step === 2), s2 = step >= 7;
    document.getElementById('scene1').classList.toggle('hidden', zoo || s2);
    document.getElementById('sceneZoo').classList.toggle('hidden', !zoo);
    document.getElementById('scene2').classList.toggle('hidden', !s2);
    document.getElementById('mwrap').classList.toggle('hidden', step !== 7);
    for(var i=0;i<NSTEP;i++) dots.children[i].className = (i===step) ? 'on' : '';
    if(zoo) drawZoo();
    else if(s2){ drawMatrices(); drawC(); }
    else { drawA(step); drawB(step); }
  }

  function setStep(n){
    n = Math.max(0, Math.min(NSTEP-1, n));
    if(n === step) return;
    step = n; render();
  }

  // ── reveal fragments own the stepping, so ←/→ walk the eight states ──
  function syncFromReveal(){
    if(!window.Reveal || !Reveal.getIndices) return;
    var idx = Reveal.getIndices();
    var f = (typeof idx.f === 'number' && !isNaN(idx.f)) ? idx.f : -1;
    setStep(f + 1);
  }
  // This script runs at parse time, before Quarto initialises Reveal, so the
  // listeners have to wait for it; the slow poll is a backstop (setStep is a
  // no-op when the step is unchanged).
  (function attach(){
    if(window.Reveal && Reveal.on && typeof Reveal.getIndices === 'function'){
      Reveal.on('fragmentshown',  syncFromReveal);
      Reveal.on('fragmenthidden', syncFromReveal);
      Reveal.on('slidechanged',   syncFromReveal);
      syncFromReveal();
      setInterval(syncFromReveal, 200);
    } else setTimeout(attach, 100);
  })();
  document.getElementById('next').onclick = function(){
    if(window.Reveal) Reveal.nextFragment(); };
  document.getElementById('prev').onclick = function(){
    if(window.Reveal) Reveal.prevFragment(); };

  // ── controls ──
  var dirty = false, redrawOnly = false;
  function markMask(){ dirty = true; }
  function markDraw(){ redrawOnly = true; }

  document.getElementById('sWidth').oninput = function(){ mW = (+this.value)/100; markMask(); };
  document.getElementById('sHoles').oninput = function(){ mH = +this.value;       markMask(); };
  document.getElementById('sApod').oninput  = function(){ mA = (+this.value)/1000; markMask(); };

  // drag the kernel along k, on either harmonic panel
  function dragTarget(svg){
    if(!svg) return;
    var down = false;
    function set(ev){
      var r = svg.getBoundingClientRect();
      var x = (ev.clientX - r.left) * (W1 / r.width);
      k0 = Math.max(12, Math.min(KMAX-12, Math.round(Bk(x))));
      markDraw();
    }
    svg.style.cursor = 'ew-resize';
    svg.addEventListener('pointerdown', function(ev){ down = true; svg.setPointerCapture(ev.pointerId); set(ev); });
    svg.addEventListener('pointermove', function(ev){ if(down) set(ev); });
    svg.addEventListener('pointerup',   function(){ down = false; });
    svg.addEventListener('pointercancel', function(){ down = false; });
  }
  dragTarget(document.getElementById('svgB'));
  dragTarget(document.getElementById('svgC'));

  // one rebuild per animation frame at most — the exact covariance and the matrix
  // inverse are real O(NK²N) / O(KP³) work and would otherwise queue behind a drag
  (function pump(){
    if(dirty){ dirty = false; redrawOnly = false; buildAll(); render(); }
    else if(redrawOnly){ redrawOnly = false; render(); }
    requestAnimationFrame(pump);
  })();

  buildAll();
  render();
  syncFromReveal();
})();
</script>
```

::: {.notes}
This is the one piece of machinery all three papers share, so it's worth ten minutes.

A Gaussian field on a line: every Fourier mode independent, covariance perfectly diagonal.
Now we only observe part of it. Note the mask isn't a box — the edges are tapered, apodized,
and that taper matters more than you'd think.

Because what the mask does in harmonic space is convolve. And the shape of that kernel is set
by the mask's *complexity*, not just its size. Here are three: a wide smoothly apodized one,
a small one, and one with holes and hard edges. Bigger and smoother buys you a narrow kernel;
holes and edges buy you a broad one with sidelobes that reach a long way. HSC-Y3 is the third
picture.

So each observed mode is a weighted sum of its neighbours within the kernel width. Take the
expectation and you get the mode-coupling matrix: the measured pseudo-spectrum is a smeared
version of the truth.

Now — and this is the thing people get wrong — that smearing is not something you approximate.
You invert it. M is exact and you compute it exactly; the decoupled estimator lands back on the
true spectrum, which is what NaMaster does and it costs you order k-cubed. **The estimator is
exact. Only its covariance is approximated.**

Because the covariance is a four-point object: a sum over a third mode of W times W-star times
C, for every pair. That's order k to the sixth, and it is genuinely intractable at Euclid
multipoles.

Hence the narrow-kernel approximation. If C barely changes across the kernel width, evaluate it
once at the midpoint of the two modes and pull it outside the sum — what's left collapses into a
single kernel, the transform of a product of masks. Drag the kernel onto the bump and watch the
number: where C is smooth the approximation is exact to a fraction of a percent, and where the
spectrum has structure on the kernel's scale it falls apart. That is the entire subject of the
first two papers.
:::

## A smaller footprint means a wider kernel {.nka-slide}

```{=html}
<div class="anim" id="s3">

<svg id="s3a" viewBox="0 0 1730 330" width="1730" height="330"></svg>
<svg id="s3b" viewBox="0 0 1730 430" width="1730" height="430"></svg>
<div class="ctl"><span id="s3n" class="big"></span><button id="s3r">replay</button></div>
</div>

<script>
(function(){
  var NS='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg';
  function el(p,t,a){var e=document.createElementNS(NS,t);for(var k in a)e.setAttribute(k,a[k]);
    p.appendChild(e);return e;}
  function txt(p,x,y,s,a){var e=el(p,'text',Object.assign({x:x,y:y,'font-size':28,
    fill:'#7A6F5C'},a||{}));e.textContent=s;return e;}

  // mask + kernel are cheap enough to build in the browser
  var NX=512, N=192;
  function mask(f){var w=new Float64Array(NX),tp=0.015*NX,h=f*NX/2,m=NX/2;
    for(var j=0;j<NX;j++){var d=Math.abs(j-m),v=0;
      if(d<=h-tp)v=1;else if(d<h+tp)v=0.5*(1+Math.cos(Math.PI*(d-h+tp)/(2*tp)));w[j]=v;}
    return w;}
  function kern(w){var p=[],mx=0;
    for(var m=-80;m<=80;m++){var sr=0,si=0;
      for(var j=0;j<NX;j++){var ph=2*Math.PI*m*j/NX;sr+=w[j]*Math.cos(ph);si-=w[j]*Math.sin(ph);}
      var v=(sr*sr+si*si)/(NX*NX);p.push(v);if(v>mx)mx=v;}
    return p.map(function(v){return v/mx;});}
  // effective coupling width: full width of the smallest symmetric window in
  // |W|^2 holding half the kernel power (same definition as the python side)
  function kwidth(k){var c=(k.length-1)/2,tot=0,i;
    for(i=0;i<k.length;i++)tot+=k[i];
    var acc=k[c],n=0;
    while(acc<0.5*tot&&n<c){n++;acc+=k[c-n]+k[c+n];}
    return Math.max(2*n,1);}

  var PAD=90, AW=1730-PAD-40;
  function drawMask(f,w){
    var s=document.getElementById('s3a');s.innerHTML='';
    var y0=56,h=230,mid=y0+h/2;
    el(s,'line',{x1:PAD,y1:mid,x2:PAD+AW,y2:mid,stroke:'#C5B89E','stroke-width':2});
    var d='';
    for(var j=0;j<NX;j++)d+=(j?'L':'M')+(PAD+AW*j/(NX-1)).toFixed(1)+' '+(mid-w[j]*h*0.40).toFixed(1)+' ';
    el(s,'path',{d:d,fill:'none',stroke:'#3D5BA0','stroke-width':4});
    var lo=PAD+AW*(0.5-f/2),hi=PAD+AW*(0.5+f/2);
    el(s,'rect',{x:lo,y:mid-h*0.40,width:hi-lo,height:h*0.40,fill:'#3D5BA0',opacity:.10});
    txt(s,PAD,y0-16,'mask  w(x)',{fill:'#3D5BA0'});
    txt(s,PAD,y0+h+34,'position  x');
  }
  function drawKernel(k){
    var s=document.getElementById('s3b');s.innerHTML='';
    var y0=34,h=300,x0=PAD;
    el(s,'line',{x1:x0,y1:y0+h,x2:x0+AW,y2:y0+h,stroke:'#C5B89E','stroke-width':2});
    var d='';
    var A=30,B=130,NP=B-A;      // show the central +-50 modes
    for(var i=A;i<=B;i++)d+=(i>A?'L':'M')+(x0+AW*(i-A)/NP).toFixed(1)+' '+(y0+h-k[i]*h).toFixed(1)+' ';
    el(s,'path',{d:d,fill:'none',stroke:'#BC4538','stroke-width':4});
    var half=kwidth(k)/2, cc=(k.length-1)/2-A;
    var lo=Math.max(cc-half,0), hi=Math.min(cc+half,NP);
    el(s,'line',{x1:x0+AW*lo/NP,y1:y0+h+26,x2:x0+AW*hi/NP,y2:y0+h+26,
                 stroke:'#BC4538','stroke-width':9,'stroke-linecap':'round'});
    txt(s,x0,y0-2,'mask kernel  |W|²',{fill:'#BC4538'});
    txt(s,x0,y0+h+74,'mode separation  k − k′');
  }

  var frames=[],i=0,timer=null;
  for(var t=0;t<28;t++){var f=0.60-(0.60-0.06)*t/27;var w=mask(f);var k=kern(w);
    frames.push({f:f,w:w,k:k,fw:kwidth(k)});}
  function show(j){var fr=frames[j];drawMask(fr.f,fr.w);drawKernel(fr.k);
    document.getElementById('s3n').textContent='kernel  '+fr.fw+' modes';}
  function play(){clearInterval(timer);i=0;show(0);
    timer=setInterval(function(){i++;if(i>=frames.length){clearInterval(timer);return;}
      show(i);},260);}
  document.getElementById('s3r').onclick=play;
  window.__jump=window.__jump||{};
  window.__jump.s3=function(j){clearInterval(timer);show(j);};
  show(0);

  var sec=document.getElementById('s3').closest('section'), was=false;
  setInterval(function(){var now=sec.classList.contains('present');
    if(now&&!was)play(); if(!now&&was)clearInterval(timer); was=now;},250);
})();
</script>
```

::: {.notes}
Quick setup beat. The mask is a top-hat and I'm shrinking it; watch the kernel underneath.
The width of the coupling kernel goes like one over the footprint width — a big contiguous
survey couples a mode only to its immediate neighbours, a small one smears across dozens.
Everything that follows is about what happens inside that width.
:::

## The diagonal is innocent {.nka-slide}

```{=html}
<div class="anim" id="s4">
<div style="display:flex; gap:44px; align-items:flex-start;">
  <div>
    <canvas id="s4m" width="96" height="96" style="width:730px;height:730px"></canvas>
    <div style="margin-top:10px; font-size:28px; color:#7A6F5C;">
      iNKA covariance &nbsp;·&nbsp; <span style="color:#1B1611;font-weight:600"
      id="s4b">bands kept</span></div>
  </div>
  <div style="flex:1;">
    <svg id="s4c" viewBox="0 0 940 730" width="940" height="730"></svg>
    <div style="font-size:28px; color:#7A6F5C; margin-left:90px;">
      separation &nbsp;θ</div>
  </div>
</div>
<div class="ctl"><button id="s4r">replay</button></div>
</div>

<script>
(function(){
  var D=window.NKA_DATA.slide4;
  var NS='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg';
  function el(p,t,a){var e=document.createElementNS(NS,t);for(var k in a)e.setAttribute(k,a[k]);
    p.appendChild(e);return e;}
  function txt(p,x,y,s,a){var e=el(p,'text',Object.assign({x:x,y:y,'font-size':28,
    fill:'#7A6F5C'},a||{}));e.textContent=s;return e;}

  var KM=D.km, bin=atob(D.matrix), M=new Uint8Array(KM*KM);
  for(var q=0;q<M.length;q++)M[q]=bin.charCodeAt(q);

  var cv=document.getElementById('s4m'), ctx=cv.getContext('2d');
  function drawMatrix(n){
    var im=ctx.createImageData(KM,KM);
    for(var i=0;i<KM;i++)for(var j=0;j<KM;j++){
      var v=M[i*KM+j]/255, inb=Math.abs(i-j)<=n, o=4*(i*KM+j), u=Math.pow(v,0.55);
      // in-band: ground -> cobalt.  outside (replaced by the exact answer): muted.
      if(inb){ im.data[o]=247-186*u; im.data[o+1]=240-149*u; im.data[o+2]=225-65*u; }
      else   { im.data[o]=247-55*u;  im.data[o+1]=240-58*u;  im.data[o+2]=225-64*u; }
      im.data[o+3]=255;
    }
    ctx.putImageData(im,0,0);
  }

  var TH=D.theta, lo=Math.log10(TH[0]), hi=Math.log10(TH[TH.length-1]);
  var X0=110, Y0=60, W=800, H=600, YLO=0.80, YHI=1.04;
  function X(t){return X0+W*(Math.log10(t)-lo)/(hi-lo);}
  function Y(r){return Y0+H*(1-(r-YLO)/(YHI-YLO));}
  function drawCurve(n){
    var s=document.getElementById('s4c');s.innerHTML='';
    for(var g=0.85;g<1.041;g+=0.05){
      el(s,'line',{x1:X0,y1:Y(g),x2:X0+W,y2:Y(g),stroke:'#E0D5BF','stroke-width':2});
      txt(s,X0-78,Y(g)+10,g.toFixed(2));
    }
    el(s,'line',{x1:X0,y1:Y(1),x2:X0+W,y2:Y(1),stroke:'#1B1611','stroke-width':3});
    txt(s,X0+W-150,Y(1)-16,'exact',{fill:'#1B1611'});
    var r=D.ratios[n],d='';
    for(var i=0;i<TH.length;i++)d+=(i?'L':'M')+X(TH[i]).toFixed(1)+' '+Y(r[i]).toFixed(1)+' ';
    el(s,'path',{d:d,fill:'none',stroke:'#BC4538','stroke-width':4});
    txt(s,X0+W-340,Y(0.815),'iNKA / exact   Cov(ξ,ξ)',{fill:'#BC4538'});
    el(s,'circle',{cx:X(TH[0]),cy:Y(r[0]),r:9,fill:'#BC4538'});
    txt(s,X(TH[0])+24,Y(r[0])-30,(100*(r[0]-1)).toFixed(1)+'%',
        {fill:'#BC4538','font-size':46,'font-weight':600});
  }

  var i=0,timer=null;
  function show(j){
    var n=D.ns[j];
    drawMatrix(n); drawCurve(j);
    document.getElementById('s4b').textContent='|k − k′| ≤ '+n;

  }
  function play(){clearInterval(timer);i=0;show(0);
    timer=setInterval(function(){i++;if(i>=D.ns.length){clearInterval(timer);return;}
      show(i);},300);}
  document.getElementById('s4r').onclick=play;
  window.__jump=window.__jump||{};
  window.__jump.s4=function(j){clearInterval(timer);show(j);};
  show(0);
  var sec=document.getElementById('s4').closest('section'), was=false;
  setInterval(function(){var now=sec.classList.contains('present');
    if(now&&!was)play(); if(!now&&was)clearInterval(timer); was=now;},250);
})();
</script>
```

::: {.notes}
This is the experiment the paper doesn't do, and it settles the diagnosis.

Start on the left with iNKA's covariance matrix, and keep only the bands within some
separation of the diagonal — everything outside, greyed, I've replaced with the exact
answer. At the start only the diagonal is iNKA's, and the real-space covariance on the
right sits on top of the truth: one percent low. So the diagonal is fine.

Now widen the band. As iNKA's own off-diagonals come back in, the curve peels away and
settles at fifteen percent low — and it gets there by about the kernel width, twenty-five
modes. Nothing outside the kernel matters.

So: iNKA is right exactly where it was fitted, the harmonic diagonal, and real space
weights precisely the part the fit never reached. And the reverse test says the same —
zero those off-diagonals instead of correcting them and you lose eighty percent of the
covariance. That band isn't a correction to the real-space covariance. It is the
real-space covariance.
:::

## Six patches, not one, is what breaks it {.nka-slide}

```{=html}
  var lo=Math.log10(C[0].theta[0]), hi=Math.log10(C[0].theta[C[0].theta.length-1]);
  var X0=110,Y0=60,W=790,H=580,YLO=0.78,YHI=1.05;
  function X(t){return X0+W*(Math.log10(t)-lo)/(hi-lo);}
  function Y(r){return Y0+H*(1-(r-YLO)/(YHI-YLO));}

</script>
```

::: {.notes}
Last beat, and it's the one that decides how much we should care.

Hold the survey area fixed at twenty percent and cut it into more pieces. One patch,
three, six — HSC-Y3 is six disjoint fields. The kernel widens five-fold, from five modes
to twenty-five, purely from the perimeter.

And the real-space error tracks it: seven percent for the contiguous mask, thirteen for
six patches. Seven percent is not a paper. Thirteen, with the wild intermediate-scale
excursions I've cut off the top of this plot, is.

So my honest reading is that this result is at least as much a statement about HSC's
geometry as about iNKA. For a contiguous Rubin-like footprint, in this toy, the problem
largely goes away — which is exactly the question the paper can't answer, because they
have one mask.
:::
